Goutam Benarji and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.

full_judgment:
2. This is an application under Section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the accused petitioners for bail in Sessions Case No.743 of 2010 arising out of G.R. No.638 of 2009 corresponding to Kotwali Police Station Case No.4 dated 3.10.2009 IV under Section 302/34 of the Penal Code now pending before the learned Sessions Judge, Mymenshing. 

 3. Short fact for disposal of this application is that the accused petitioners were granted bail by a Division Bench of this country by its order dated 10.6.2010 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 11145 of 2010 considering the merit of the case and the accused petitioners were enjoying privilege of bail without misusing the same. Subsequently the learned Sessions Judge, Mymenshing was pleased to grant bail to the accused petitioners by his order dated 15.11.2010 and 5.1.2011. Thereafter the informant filed an application for cancellation of bail of the accused petitioners and after hearing the learned Advocates for the parties the learned Sessions Judge, Mymenshing was pleased to grant regular bail to one Gopal Benarji, as he is an ailing man, but cancelled the bail of the present accused petitioners and remanded them to custody. In canceling the bail he hai considered that there is an allegation in the F.I.R. against the accused petitioners and without assigning any other reasons whatsoever, the learned Sessions Judge cancelled the bail of the accused petitioners arbitrarily. 

 4. We have heard the learned Advocate for the accused petitioners and the learned Deputy Attorney General for the State and perused the records. We are surprised to note that once the bail of the accused petitioners has been granted by the learned Judges of High Court considering the merit of the case, the Sessions Judge has no scope to re-assess the merit of the said case once again. Further the impugned order does not reflect the fact that the accused persons have misused the privilege of bail in any manner whatsoever. But merely on an application filed by the informant it cannot be considered that the accused petitioners have misused the privilege of bail. The learned Judges of the High Court Division in its bail granting order clearly held that the trial Court will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the accused petitioners if they misuse the privilege of bail or tampering or threatening the witnesses to depose in this case. In this case no trial has yet been started. Moreover, the application which has been filed by the informant has not been referred in the impugned order as a cause of canceling the bail of the accused persons. 

 6. The Apex Courts of the Sub-continent formulated some grounds and procedure in respect of cancellation of bail such as if any application for cancellation of bail is received by court, the court will start a separate miscellaneous case for cancellation of bail and serve notice upon the accused persons, giving them sufficient time to explain their conduct and at the same time the informant party or the applicant be asked to produce witness in support of his allegation and the accused persons must be allowed to cross examine the witnesses proposed to be examined in support of the allegation of cancellation of bail and thereafter the court will arrive at a decision as to whether the accused persons have misused the privilege of bail or threatened the witnesses or obstructed the witnesses in coming to the court to depose. Otherwise the court cannot cancel the bail arbitrarily. 

 11. However, the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail of the accused petitioner in case of misuse the privilege of bail after observing legal formalities as observed above.
